```{=html}
<div class="about-grid"><figure class="about-photo"><img src="assets/qing-han.jpg" alt="Portrait of Qing Han" width="620" height="826"><figcaption>Qing Han · 韩晴</figcaption></figure><div class="about-text"><h2>Research & practice</h2><p>I am a researcher working at the intersection of anthropology, history, and science and technology studies. I study how categories of knowledge, personhood, and value are made and contested, and how they become consequential through technologies and institutions.</p><p>I hold an MSc in Social Anthropology from the University of Oxford and a BA in Social Sciences from King’s College London. My Oxford dissertation developed the concept of <em>fantamacy</em> (fantasy intimacy) through ethnographic research on mengnü culture and Chinese otome-game fandoms.</p><p>My projects follow these questions into different settings: aging and care technologies; commercial and investment visions of the future; <a href="research/hongshan.html">translation as governance in Hongshan heritage work</a>; and changing definitions of good talent in an era of AI recruitment. Across them, I ask who gets to define a need, establish a standard, or decide what counts as evidence.</p><p>Historical inquiry helps me examine how these categories came to seem natural and how their meanings have changed. Ethnography brings me close to the decisions, relationships, and frictions through which they are sustained or contested.</p><p>I translated <a href="writing/ancient-hongshan-kingdom.html"><em>The Ancient Hongshan Kingdom</em> (红山古国)</a>, a published children’s picture book introducing Hongshan cultural heritage to English-language readers.</p><p>Alongside research, I work in cultural heritage translation and AI product development. These roles bring me into practical decisions about language, design, and evidence. They also require attention to my own position: participating in a project gives me a perspective on its work, while the use of that experience as research requires a separate account of methods and responsibilities.</p><a class="text-link" href="cv.html">View my CV <span aria-hidden="true">↗</span></a><div class="contact-block"><p class="eyebrow">Contact</p><a href="mailto:qinghan.research@gmail.com">qinghan.research@gmail.com</a></div></div></div><section class="interests"><p class="eyebrow">Intellectual interests</p><div class="interest-tags"><span>Historical anthropology of technology</span><span>Science & technology studies</span><span>Markets, finance & valuation</span><span>Aging & care</span><span>Intimacy & digital culture</span><span>Classification, work & AI</span><span>Cultural heritage</span></div></section>
```
